ambiguities.description: Objectification of Enrollment: The transcript states that students receive grades for course offerings they are enrolled in, but does not explicitly state that 'Enrollment' should be treated as a named entity with its own properties. While objectification is a reasonable inference (Enrollment needs a reference mode to capture the grade-to-enrollment relationship), the university system documentation should clarify whether Enrollment is formally a business object with its own tracking, or whether grades are simply recorded on the Student-CourseOffering relationship without a separate Enrollment entity.

source_references.excerpt: At the end of a semester, a student receives a letter grade for each course offering they were enrolled in. A student gets at most one grade per offering.

ambiguities.description: Enrollment reference mode: If Enrollment is objectified, what is its reference identifier? The transcript does not specify how enrollments are uniquely identified. Are they identified by the combination of (Student, CourseOffering), or do they have a separate enrollment ID?

source_references.excerpt: At the end of a semester, a student receives a letter grade for each course offering they were enrolled in.

ambiguities.description: Optional participation in grading: The transcript states 'a student receives a letter grade for each course offering they were enrolled in,' implying that enrolled students eventually receive grades. However, it is unclear whether all enrolled students receive grades by the end of the semester, or whether grade assignment is optional (e.g., if a student drops before grading).

ambiguities.description: Mandatory participation in enrollment: The transcript does not clarify whether every student must enroll in at least one course, or whether a student can exist in the system without any enrollments.

However, it is unclear whether there are any upper limits on the number of offerings an instructor may teach, or whether this is constrained in practice.

It is unclear whether values outside this range (0, 7, or higher) are possible exceptions or strictly forbidden.
